Determine the following fields:
- `bilingual`: Read the README (or at least the first few hundred lines). Does it contain meaningful content in both English and French? Look for French words/phrases, French section headers, or a clear French translation. Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`Unknown`.
- `readme_clarity`: Read the README. Does it clearly explain what the project is, who it's for, and how to use it? `Poor`/`Fair`/`Good`/`Unknown`.
- `security_policy`: Check for `SECURITY.md` in root, `.github/`, and `docs/`. If not found, write `Missing`. If found, read it. If it contains real responsible disclosure instructions (contact info, how to report, PGP key, etc.), write `Present`. If it exists but is just a placeholder or links without real instructions, write `Incomplete`. Allowed: `Present`/`Incomplete`/`Missing`/`Unknown`.
- `issue_response_quality`: Look at the 5 most recently updated open issues (API `issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc`, filter out PRs). For each, check if anyone other than the original reporter commented within the last 6 months (from 2026-07-13). If at least one issue has such a comment, write `Active`. If none, write `Stale`. If there are no open issues, write `No Issues`. Allowed: `Active`/`Stale`/`No Issues`/`Unknown`.
- `release_notes_quality`: Check the Releases page (API `releases` or HTML). If no releases, write `No Releases`. If releases exist, check the latest few. # Algorithmic Impact Assessment (.NET)

This project will host a prototype of the next iteration of the Algorithmic Impact Assessment (AIA) developed using C# and the .NET framework.

It will consist in two main capabilities:

* Offer a simple interface for the administrative team to update the questionnaire's questions, answers and scoring mechanism
* Offer a web-based questionnaire for end-users to assess their automated decision-making system

The AIA is a critical piece of the [Directive on Automated Decision-Making](http://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32592) and we want to ensure its development is done in the open.

The users of this project will be Government of Canada employees assessing the impact of using an automated decision system, including Artificial Intelligence, as part of their programs and services.

As this assessment tool is open source, other countries and individiuals may wish to also leverage it and even contribute back to it.

# Évaluation de l'incidence algorithmique (.NET)

Ce projet accueillera un prototype de la prochaine itération de l'étude d'impact algorithmique (EIA) développé en C# et en utilisant le framework .NET.

Il se composera de deux capacités principales :

* Offrir une interface simple permettant à l'équipe administrative de mettre à jour les questions, les réponses et le mécanisme de notation du questionnaire.
* Proposer un questionnaire en ligne aux utilisateurs finaux pour évaluer leur système automatisé de prise de décision.

L'EAI est un élément essentiel de la [Directive sur la prise de décision automatisée](http://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32592) et nous voulons nous assurer que son élaboration se fasse au grand jour.
